events.title: Russian occupation during the Thirteen Years' War
hints: A tsar's armies seized Smolensk and Vitebsk in the mid-17th century.
The long war left the country's towns and countryside heavily devastated.
events.summary: During the Russo-Polish War of 1654–67, Muscovite forces occupied large parts of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, including Smolensk, Vitebsk and Minsk. The war and accompanying epidemics devastated the territory; estimates of population loss vary widely.

events.title: Russian annexation in the Partitions
hints: Three carve-ups of a neighbouring commonwealth moved the eastern borderlands under the tsars.
The last gains in 1795 completed the absorption.
events.summary: In the Partitions of Poland, Russia annexed eastern Belarus in 1772, much of the centre in 1793 and the west in 1795. The lands became governorates of the Russian Empire, with serfdom and the Orthodox church favoured by the state.

events.title: Russification and abolition of the Uniate Church
hints: A church synod in 1839 absorbed a Greek Catholic church into the state Orthodox one.
After an 1863 uprising the use of the national language in schools and print was suppressed.
events.summary: In 1839 the Synod of Polotsk dissolved the Uniate Church in the region and incorporated it into the Russian Orthodox Church. After the 1863 uprising, Russification policies in the Northwestern Krai restricted the use of local languages in education and print.

events.title: German occupation under Ober Ost
hints: A military state in the east was run by the army from 1915.
The ancient forest of Bialowieza was heavily logged for the war effort.
events.summary: From 1915 German forces occupied western Belarus, which was administered by the military authority Ober Ost. The occupiers requisitioned grain, logged the forests including Bialowieza and conscripted labourers until the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk and the armistice.

events.title: Soviet offensive and conquest of the Belarusian People's Republic
hints: As German garrisons withdrew in late 1918, another army moved into the vacuum from the east.
A republic proclaimed in March 1918 never won international recognition and was driven from its capital.
A Soviet republic was proclaimed in early January 1919.
events.summary: As Ober Ost garrisons withdrew after the First World War, Soviet Russia advanced west in the 1918-1919 westward offensive. The Red Army took Minsk in December 1918, conquering the Belarusian People's Republic proclaimed in March 1918, and a Soviet republic was proclaimed in January 1919.

events.title: Polish rule over western Belarus
hints: A treaty signed at Riga in 1921 divided the territory between two neighbours.
Schools teaching in the local language were gradually closed during the 1920s and 1930s.
events.summary: The Peace of Riga in March 1921 divided the area between Poland and Soviet Russia, and Poland ruled the western part until 1939. Polish settlement, land policy and school policy limited local cultural life, and the area was known as the Kresy.

events.title: Kurapaty executions
hints: A forest on the edge of the capital became a burial site for victims of the secret police.
events.summary: In the Great Purge and after, the Soviet secret police shot large numbers of people and buried them at Kurapaty near Minsk. Estimates of the number of victims start at around 30,000 and remain disputed, and the graves were publicised in 1988.

events.title: Soviet invasion and annexation of the west
hints: On 17 September 1939 an army crossed the eastern border of a neighbour already under attack from the west.
A staged election in October 1939 led to annexation.
events.summary: Following the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, the Red Army invaded eastern Poland on 17 September 1939 and took western Belarus. After staged elections the region was annexed to the Belarusian SSR, and tens of thousands were deported in 1940–41.

events.title: Nazi German occupation
hints: A war of annihilation from 1941 destroyed hundreds of villages and killed about a quarter of the population.
A memorial at Khatyn recalls villagers burned alive in a barn.
events.summary: Germany occupied the territory from June 1941 until the Red Army's Operation Bagration in 1944. About a quarter of the population died, including most of the Jewish community, and hundreds of villages were destroyed in anti-partisan operations.
events.wikipediaTitle: Occupation of Belarus by Nazi Germany
